159/160/164/169 use geographic references in differing comparisons. Personal/geographic microheadings are not automatic, but Ireland, America and the Nootka dispute have meaningful contextual or whole-book routes that must not be excluded.
160–161 anonymous testimony remains substantive reception evidence without requiring invented named biographies.
Brief identifying mentions need not each become weighted units; this is conditional on preserving useful events, roles and reader access, not an exclusion of listed pages.

160 lists German intellectual reactions and skeptical exceptions. Preserve the contrast and Clootz’s distinct developed activity; do not infer that only a recurring name could ever merit personal access.
160–161 contain Swedish/Russian enthusiasm; correct page list to include Stroganov’s continuation on 161. Personal weighting remains optional for these quotations.
161 witness/statistical details establish reception and exile patterns. Preserve their substantive scale and interpretation without additional biography/number units.

162 grain shortage helps drive hungry urban crowds behind anti-Austrian opposition. Independent famine weighting is optional only if this causal comparison with France remains within Brabant Revolution access.

164 peasant September Crusade is an identifiable failed resistance component of Austrian reconquest. Preserve subordinate event access and the reconquest sequence; independent conceptual weighting is unnecessary.
164–165 the Pacific setting and Spanish territorial claim explain Nootka’s diplomatic test. No extra geographic survey is needed, but the rival claim and dynastic-alliance controversy must survive.

166 Polish Friends of the Constitution demonstrates borrowed French forms within a substantially different constitutional project. Retain the club identification and superficial-parallel qualification within Polish reform.

167–169 rhetorical people/social labels belong to arguments about hereditary right, liberty, aristocracy and generational autonomy. They do not automatically create personal units, but their conceptual distinctions remain eligible.
169 comparative book sales and anniversary celebration show reach and mobilization, not decorative numbers. Keep them in the controversy/radical revival route without separate numerical headings.

170 Pétion’s visit illustrates transnational fraternity, and the royal song’s success reflects loyalist reaction after Varennes. Preserve both opposed forms of mobilization even without separate event/song units.
171 grouped German patrons support émigré subsidy and preparation. Retain subsidy/international refuge routes and distinctions for Trier/Mainz when developed elsewhere.
172 registration is a concrete coercive instrument of Spanish containment. Independent demographic group weighting is optional; surveillance of foreigners must remain within policy access.
Parent DEFD meaning/access explicitly retain Bastille liberation and European interpretation; consolidation is viable, conditional on final preservation of the distinct component.
Parent DEFD expressly retains surprise, celebration and intellectual/public reception. No extra weighted duplicate is needed; locality and constituency differences must survive final repair.
Parent DEFD includes changing uncertainty and alarm, with access to foreign disillusionment. Keep uneven chronology and the distinct British revival rather than implying universal linear decline.
Parent 943186 meaning and stance explicitly distinguish Catherine’s Polish aims from an anti-French crusade. This is a coherent component, not an exclusion of the policy.
174 has a substantive display title; exclude only running heads/page numerals and the bare chapter number. Correct the historical title-as-furniture decision rather than importing it.
Bare note callouts are apparatus; the existing explicit protection of substantive body text and quotations is correct.

174/176/180/183/192/193/195 identifying names do not automatically create biographies. Preserve the guillotine’s origin, massacre victims, convention composition and trial defense; independently developed actors remain eligible elsewhere.

177–179/182–183/192 place references support war, émigré activity, provisioning and regional violence. Retain meaningful distinctions such as competing southern cities, not a blanket geographic exclusion.

175/177/182–184 distinguish refractory policy, food riot, anti-seigneurial attacks and wartime panic. These speakers/officials are not all attribution only: retain their actions, with separate biographies optional.

Secondary ministers and Girondin associates retain distinct functions through ministry, war and trial routes. No local duplicate biography is required; this cannot exclude Vergniaud’s or others’ developed treatment elsewhere.
Clootz, Chaumette and Roux are substantive whole-book political actors. Local nonduplication may stand only with the exact internationalist/popular-radical content and whole-book access retained.

193–194 foreign/notable election examples illustrate Convention composition. Preserve international associations and the distinction between those elected and those who actually came, without mandatory separate election biographies.

195 de Sèze’s argument about circumstance and the king’s claimed grant of liberty belongs in trial access. A separate counsel biography is optional, but the substantive defense is not merely an attribution.

175/186/192/193 eyewitnesses provide interpretations of emigration, constitutional crisis, volunteering and Valmy. Retain the content and the retrospective character of the world-historical interpretation without extra biographies.
177 and related war-origin pages make Trier/Mainz protections and threatened pressure substantive causes. Separate polity biographies are unnecessary here, not the diplomatic mechanism itself.
